texts.preamble: Ravindra Tiwari vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 4 August, 2023 Author: Deepak Verma Bench: Deepak Verma High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:157263 Court No. - 89 Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 43436 of 2013 Applicant :- Ravindra Tiwari Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Anr. Counsel for Applicant :- Sameer Jain,Vikash Bhatnagar
texts.facts: The FIR was lodged against the applicant in Case No.106 of 2010 (State Vs. Ravindra Tiwari), under sections 272, 273, IPC and section 7/11 Food Adulteration Act, and also Complaint Case No.1521 of 2010 (State Vs. Ravindra Tiwariand others), under section 7/16 Food Adulteration Act. He next submits that the Complaint Case No.1521 of 2010 (State Vs. Ravindra Ravindra Tiwari vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61848637/ 1 Tiwariand others), under section 7/16 Food Adulteration Act, was decided by the trial court vide order dated 08.02.2013 and acquitted the applicant under section 7/16 Food Adulteration Act. Now the proceeding of Case No.106 of 2010 (State Vs. Ravindra Tiwari), under sections 272, 273, IPC and section 7/11 Food Adulteration Act, is pending.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that two proceedings lodged against the applicant for the same allegations. Counsel for the applicant placed reliance of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court passed in the case of "Harish Vs. State of U.P. and others", in which the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "refusal of quashing the prosecution under impugned order passed by the High Court is challenged on the same facts a prosecution under section 7/16 of the PFA Act was launched against the appellant and the said proceedings have ended in acquittal on the finding that the food item was not kept for sale, the Supreme Court held that in view of the finding recorded in the proceeding under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, the prosecution under IPC is bound to be a lame/sham prosecution".
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that two proceedings lodged against the applicant for the same allegations. Counsel for the applicant placed reliance of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court passed in the case of "Harish Vs. State of U.P. and others", in which the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "refusal of quashing the prosecution under impugned order passed by the High Court is challenged on the same facts a prosecution under section 7/16 of the PFA Act was launched against the appellant and the said proceedings have ended in acquittal on the finding that the food item was not kept for sale, the Supreme Court held that in view of the finding recorded in the proceeding under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, the prosecution under IPC is bound to be a lame/sham prosecution".
